headline: Researchers built EnhancerDetector, a deep-learning tool that spots enhancers, the DNA stretches that switch genes on and off, in organisms from humans to fruit flies using only the DNA sequence.
score_reason: Good cross-species results and a small lab check, but only six candidates were tested and no outside review is reported.
importance_line: Genome researchers could annotate new genomes faster, though the lab check covered only six candidate sequences and the tool is pitched as a first-stage aid.
summary: Scienmag, as relayed by Bioengineer.org, reports on a BMC Genomics study in which a model trained on human DNA outperformed existing methods on human, mouse and fly data, and of six fly candidates it predicted, five drove a glowing reporter gene in living flies, four of them matching earlier findings. The authors present it as a first-stage tool for annotating newly sequenced genomes, not a replacement for experiments.
notes: Article carries Scienmag's text (credited at the end); Scienmag named as source. Only six fly candidates were tested.
